paragraphs.title: Joseph Presents His Family to Pharaoh

easy.question: Who told Pharaoh that Joseph’s family had arrived in Egypt?
easy.explanation: Joseph came to Pharaoh and told him that his father, brothers, and all they owned had come from Canaan.

easy.question: Where did Joseph’s brothers ask to live?
easy.explanation: The brothers asked Pharaoh to let them settle in the land of Goshen.

easy.question: What was the occupation of the brothers and their ancestors?
easy.explanation: The brothers said that they were shepherds, as their ancestors had been.

medium.question: Why did the brothers ask to live in the land of Goshen?
answers: There was no pasture for their flocks in Canaan
Pharaoh ordered them to live there
medium.explanation: The severe famine left no pasture for their flocks in Canaan, so they asked to live in Goshen.

medium.question: What happened after Joseph told Pharaoh that his family was in Goshen?
answers: Pharaoh immediately sent them back to Canaan
Joseph presented five of his brothers to Pharaoh
The brothers appointed Joseph as a governor
medium.explanation: After speaking to Pharaoh, Joseph took five of his brothers and presented them to him.

medium.question: In the verse “For to sojourn in the land are we come,” what does “sojourn” mean?
medium.explanation: The brothers had come because of the famine and asked to dwell in Egypt as temporary residents.

challenge.question: What additional option did Pharaoh offer besides giving the family a place to live?
answers: Appointing capable men among them as overseers of his cattle
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh offered to appoint capable men among them as rulers over his cattle.

challenge.question: Why did Pharaoh think the brothers could manage his cattle?
answers: They were members of the royal family
They had experience and skill as shepherds
They knew how to read and write
challenge.explanation: The brothers said that they had been shepherds for generations, so Pharaoh saw that they might manage livestock well.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ statement that they were shepherds, “both we, and also our fathers”?
answers: They wanted to hide their occupation
challenge.explanation: Their words show that shepherding had been passed down in the family from generation to generation.

questions.question: What additional option did Pharaoh offer besides giving the family a place to live?
answers: Appointing capable men among them as overseers of his cattle
questions.explanation: Pharaoh offered to appoint capable men among them as rulers over his cattle.

questions.question: Why did Pharaoh think the brothers could manage his cattle?
answers: They were members of the royal family
They had experience and skill as shepherds
They knew how to read and write
questions.explanation: The brothers said that they had been shepherds for generations, so Pharaoh saw that they might manage livestock well.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ statement that they were shepherds, “both we, and also our fathers”?
answers: They wanted to hide their occupation
questions.explanation: Their words show that shepherding had been passed down in the family from generation to generation.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Blesses Pharaoh and Israel’s Family Settles in Rameses

easy.question: Who brought Jacob before Pharaoh?
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joseph brought his father Jacob and set him before Pharaoh.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh ask Jacob?
easy.explanation: Pharaoh asked Jacob, “How old art thou?”

easy.question: What did Joseph give his family in Egypt?
answers: A possession in the land of Rameses
easy.explanation: Joseph settled his father and brothers in Rameses, the best part of the land.

medium.question: What did Jacob do after blessing Pharaoh?
answers: He went back to his brothers
medium.explanation: At the end of the meeting, Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from before him.

medium.question: Why did Jacob say that his days had been “few and evil”?
answers: He had lived only a few years and had no children
His life had been relatively short and full of troubles
He did not want to live in Egypt
medium.explanation: Jacob said his years were fewer than those of his ancestors and had been filled with hardship.

medium.question: In the phrase “The days of the years of my pilgrimage,” what does “pilgrimage” refer to?
answers: His years of wandering and living as a sojourner
medium.explanation: Jacob was describing his years of life as a person who had lived and wandered through the world.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Joseph nourished “all his father’s household”?
answers: Joseph provided for his entire family
Joseph gave food only to his brothers
challenge.explanation: The passage expands Joseph’s care from his father and brothers to everyone in his father’s household.

challenge.question: What does the fact that Jacob blessed Pharaoh both at the beginning and at the end of the meeting emphasize?
answers: That the meeting was very long
That the blessing was central to the meeting
That Pharaoh asked Jacob to leave
challenge.explanation: The blessing appears when Jacob enters and when he leaves, framing the meeting and emphasizing its importance.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the fact that Joseph gave his family Rameses “as Pharaoh had commanded”?
answers: Joseph carried out Pharaoh’s order and gave them a good place
challenge.explanation: The passage says both that Rameses was among the best land and that Joseph acted according to Pharaoh’s command.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Joseph nourished “all his father’s household”?
answers: Joseph provided for his entire family
Joseph gave food only to his brothers
questions.explanation: The passage expands Joseph’s care from his father and brothers to everyone in his father’s household.

questions.question: What does the fact that Jacob blessed Pharaoh both at the beginning and at the end of the meeting emphasize?
answers: That the meeting was very long
That the blessing was central to the meeting
That Pharaoh asked Jacob to leave
questions.explanation: The blessing appears when Jacob enters and when he leaves, framing the meeting and emphasizing its importance.

questions.question: What can be learned from the fact that Joseph gave his family Rameses “as Pharaoh had commanded”?
answers: Joseph carried out Pharaoh’s order and gave them a good place
questions.explanation: The passage says both that Rameses was among the best land and that Joseph acted according to Pharaoh’s command.

paragraphs.title: The Severe Famine and the Emptying of the People’s Money

easy.question: What was lacking throughout the land because of the famine?
easy.explanation: The passage says that there was no bread in all the land.

easy.question: What did Joseph collect from Egypt and Canaan?
easy.explanation: Joseph gathered all the money found in Egypt and Canaan in exchange for food.

easy.question: What did Joseph give the people in exchange for their livestock?
easy.explanation: The Egyptians brought their livestock, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange.

medium.question: Why did the Egyptians bring their livestock to Joseph?
answers: They had run out of money and wanted bread
Joseph ordered them to surrender their livestock
medium.explanation: After their money ran out, the Egyptians asked for bread and offered their livestock in exchange.

medium.question: In the phrase “Give your cattle,” what does “cattle” mean?
medium.explanation: Here, “cattle” means the livestock they owned, including horses, flocks, herds, and asses.

medium.question: What did Joseph do with the money he collected?
answers: He gave it to the poor
He brought it into Pharaoh’s house
medium.explanation: The passage says that Joseph brought all the money into Pharaoh’s house.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that all Egypt and Canaan came to Joseph to buy food?
answers: Joseph had a central role in controlling the distribution of food
The Egyptians received bread without paying
challenge.explanation: Everyone came to Joseph, who supplied bread in exchange for money and livestock, giving him central control over food distribution.

challenge.question: Which animal is not mentioned in the list of livestock brought to Joseph?
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions horses, flocks, herds, and asses, but not camels.

challenge.question: What does the change from payment in money to payment in livestock reveal about the Egyptians’ situation?
answers: They preferred to save their money
Livestock was worth more than bread
Their other means of payment had run out, and famine forced them to surrender their property
challenge.explanation: They first paid with money, but when it was gone, they offered their livestock to obtain food.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that all Egypt and Canaan came to Joseph to buy food?
answers: Joseph had a central role in controlling the distribution of food
The Egyptians received bread without paying
questions.explanation: Everyone came to Joseph, who supplied bread in exchange for money and livestock, giving him central control over food distribution.

questions.question: Which animal is not mentioned in the list of livestock brought to Joseph?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions horses, flocks, herds, and asses, but not camels.

questions.question: What does the change from payment in money to payment in livestock reveal about the Egyptians’ situation?
answers: They preferred to save their money
Livestock was worth more than bread
Their other means of payment had run out, and famine forced them to surrender their property
questions.explanation: They first paid with money, but when it was gone, they offered their livestock to obtain food.

paragraphs.title: The People Give Their Lands to Pharaoh

easy.question: Who bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh?
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh.

easy.question: What remained for the Egyptians after their money and livestock were gone?
easy.explanation: The Egyptians told Joseph that nothing remained except their bodies and their land.

easy.question: Whose land did Joseph not buy?
easy.explanation: The passage specifically says that Joseph did not buy the land of the priests.

medium.question: What did the Egyptians do after both their money and livestock were gone?
answers: They offered to sell themselves and their land for bread
They asked the priests for their land
medium.explanation: After losing their money and livestock, the Egyptians asked Joseph to buy them and their land in exchange for food.

medium.question: In the phrase “that the land be not desolate,” what does “desolate” mean?
medium.explanation: They asked for seed so they could live and work the land rather than leave it empty and abandoned.

medium.question: Why did the priests not sell their land?
answers: They did not suffer from the famine
They hid their land from Joseph
Pharaoh gave them an allowance of food
medium.explanation: The priests had an allowance from Pharaoh, so they received food and did not need to sell their land.

challenge.question: What was the main change in land ownership after the famine?
answers: Most of Egypt’s land passed to Pharaoh
All the land passed to the priests
The land was redistributed among the farmers
challenge.explanation: Because the Egyptians sold their fields, the land became Pharaoh’s, except for the priests’ land.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Joseph moving the people to cities throughout Egypt?
answers: The Egyptians wanted to abandon farming permanently
Joseph reorganized Egypt’s population under central authority
The priests demanded that everyone move to one city
challenge.explanation: Moving the people from one end of Egypt to the other suggests a reorganization under Pharaoh’s centralized rule.

challenge.question: What distinction remained between the people and the priests after the famine?
answers: The people received seed, while the priests received money
The people kept their land, while the priests lost theirs
The people sold their land to Pharaoh, while the priests kept theirs
challenge.explanation: The people had to sell their land because of the famine, but the priests kept theirs because of the food allowance they received from Pharaoh.

questions.question: What was the main change in land ownership after the famine?
answers: Most of Egypt’s land passed to Pharaoh
All the land passed to the priests
The land was redistributed among the farmers
questions.explanation: Because the Egyptians sold their fields, the land became Pharaoh’s, except for the priests’ land.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Joseph moving the people to cities throughout Egypt?
answers: The Egyptians wanted to abandon farming permanently
Joseph reorganized Egypt’s population under central authority
The priests demanded that everyone move to one city
questions.explanation: Moving the people from one end of Egypt to the other suggests a reorganization under Pharaoh’s centralized rule.

questions.question: What distinction remained between the people and the priests after the famine?
answers: The people received seed, while the priests received money
The people kept their land, while the priests lost theirs
The people sold their land to Pharaoh, while the priests kept theirs
questions.explanation: The people had to sell their land because of the famine, but the priests kept theirs because of the food allowance they received from Pharaoh.

paragraphs.title: The Fifth-Part Law and the Renewal of the Land

easy.question: What did Joseph give the people so they could sow the land?
easy.explanation: Joseph said, “Lo, here is seed for you,” so they could plant the land.

easy.question: What portion of the harvest did they have to give Pharaoh?
easy.explanation: Joseph established that the people would give one-fifth of the produce to Pharaoh.

easy.question: Who did not have to give up their land to Pharaoh?
easy.explanation: The passage says that only the priests’ land did not become Pharaoh’s.

medium.question: Why did Joseph give the people seed after buying them and their land for Pharaoh?
answers: So they could sow the land and grow crops
medium.explanation: Joseph enabled the people to restore farming and grow food after the years of famine.

medium.question: In the phrase “ye shall give the fifth part unto Pharaoh,” what does “fifth part” mean?
medium.explanation: A fifth part is one out of five; the remaining four parts belonged to the people.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: The people thanked Joseph, and only afterward received seed
Joseph established the law, and only afterward bought the land
Joseph bought the people and their land, gave them seed, and established the division of the harvest
medium.explanation: First Joseph acquired the people and their land for Pharaoh, then gave them seed, and finally established the division of the harvest.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the people saying, “Thou hast saved our lives”?
answers: They viewed Joseph as the one who rescued them from the famine
They wanted Joseph to be king
They refused to accept the seed
challenge.explanation: Their words express gratitude because Joseph gave them a way to survive and obtain food during the crisis.

challenge.question: What did it mean that Joseph left the people four parts out of five?
answers: Pharaoh received most of the harvest
The people retained most of the harvest for various needs
The people no longer had to work the land
challenge.explanation: After giving one-fifth to Pharaoh, the people kept four parts for seed, food, and their households.

challenge.question: What special feature distinguished the priests’ land from the rest of Egypt’s land?
answers: The priests received twice the usual fifth
Their land did not belong to Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the priests’ land alone did not become Pharaoh’s.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the people saying, “Thou hast saved our lives”?
answers: They viewed Joseph as the one who rescued them from the famine
They wanted Joseph to be king
They refused to accept the seed
questions.explanation: Their words express gratitude because Joseph gave them a way to survive and obtain food during the crisis.

questions.question: What did it mean that Joseph left the people four parts out of five?
answers: Pharaoh received most of the harvest
The people retained most of the harvest for various needs
The people no longer had to work the land
questions.explanation: After giving one-fifth to Pharaoh, the people kept four parts for seed, food, and their households.

questions.question: What special feature distinguished the priests’ land from the rest of Egypt’s land?
answers: The priests received twice the usual fifth
Their land did not belong to Pharaoh
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that the priests’ land alone did not become Pharaoh’s.

paragraphs.title: Israel Prospers in the Land of Goshen

easy.question: In what land did Israel live?
easy.explanation: The passage says that Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt.

easy.question: In what region of Egypt did Israel live?
easy.explanation: Israel lived in Egypt, in the country of Goshen.

easy.question: How old was Jacob when he died?
easy.explanation: The passage says that the whole age of Jacob was 147 years.

medium.question: What happened to Israel’s family in the land of Goshen?
medium.explanation: The passage says that they had possessions there and grew and multiplied exceedingly.

medium.question: In the phrase “they had possessions therein,” what does “had possessions” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that Israel’s family became established in Goshen rather than merely passing through.

medium.question: What order of events is described?
answers: Jacob died, and then the family came to Egypt
The family left Goshen, and then it multiplied
Israel lived in Goshen, multiplied, and Jacob lived many years in Egypt
medium.explanation: The passage first describes Israel’s settlement and growth in Goshen, then Jacob’s years in Egypt.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the statement that Israel “had possessions” in Goshen?
answers: They regarded Goshen as a settled home
They stayed in Goshen for only one day
They were not allowed to live in Goshen
challenge.explanation: The statement shows that Israel’s family became established in Goshen, not merely temporary visitors.

challenge.question: How many years did Jacob live in Egypt?
challenge.explanation: The passage states that Jacob lived in Egypt for seventeen years.

challenge.question: What is the significance of the connection between Israel’s growth and Jacob’s years in Egypt?
answers: The passage describes only Pharaoh’s age
It says Jacob lived in Egypt before his family arrived
It presents both the family’s prosperity and the final period of Jacob’s life
challenge.explanation: Together, the verses describe Israel’s success in Egypt and Jacob’s seventeen years there.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that Israel “had possessions” in Goshen?
answers: They regarded Goshen as a settled home
They stayed in Goshen for only one day
They were not allowed to live in Goshen
questions.explanation: The statement shows that Israel’s family became established in Goshen, not merely temporary visitors.

questions.question: How many years did Jacob live in Egypt?
questions.explanation: The passage states that Jacob lived in Egypt for seventeen years.

questions.question: What is the significance of the connection between Israel’s growth and Jacob’s years in Egypt?
answers: The passage describes only Pharaoh’s age
It says Jacob lived in Egypt before his family arrived
It presents both the family’s prosperity and the final period of Jacob’s life
questions.explanation: Together, the verses describe Israel’s success in Egypt and Jacob’s seventeen years there.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Makes Joseph Swear to Bury Him in Canaan

easy.question: Whom did Israel call and ask for help?
easy.explanation: Israel called Joseph, his son, and asked him to fulfill his request.

easy.question: What did Israel ask them not to do after his death?
easy.explanation: Israel asked Joseph, “Bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt.”

easy.question: What did Joseph promise Israel?
answers: That he would remain in Egypt
That he would build him a house
That he would do as he had said
easy.explanation: Joseph said, “I will do as thou hast said,” agreeing to fulfill his father’s request.

medium.question: Why did Israel turn specifically to Joseph with his request?
answers: Joseph was his son and held authority in Egypt
medium.explanation: Joseph was Israel’s son and held an important position in Egypt, so he could arrange the burial.

medium.question: In the phrase “deal kindly and truly with me,” what does it mean to deal “kindly and truly”?
answers: To show faithful and dependable kindness
medium.explanation: Israel asked Joseph for a faithful favor: to arrange his burial in the land of his ancestors.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Joseph buried Israel, and then Israel asked for help
Israel moved to Egypt, and then asked to remain there
Israel asked Joseph to bury him with his ancestors, and Joseph agreed
medium.explanation: Israel first asked Joseph to promise to carry him from Egypt, and Joseph then agreed to do so.

challenge.question: What can be learned from Israel’s request to be buried with his ancestors rather than in Egypt?
answers: He considered himself connected to his ancestral land
He wanted Joseph to become king
challenge.explanation: The request expresses Israel’s connection to his family and ancestral land, even though he lived in Egypt.

challenge.question: What was the significance of Israel asking Joseph to put his hand under his thigh?
answers: He was asking for help walking
It emphasized a solemn oath or commitment
It signaled that Joseph should leave Egypt
challenge.explanation: The gesture was part of a solemn pledge and emphasized that Israel wanted a binding promise.

challenge.question: What is the difference between “I will lie with my fathers” and “bury me in their buryingplace”?
answers: The first refers to death, and the second to burial
The first refers to the journey, and the second to the oath
challenge.explanation: “Lie with my fathers” is a respectful reference to death, while the second phrase describes burial with the ancestors.

questions.question: What can be learned from Israel’s request to be buried with his ancestors rather than in Egypt?
answers: He considered himself connected to his ancestral land
He wanted Joseph to become king
questions.explanation: The request expresses Israel’s connection to his family and ancestral land, even though he lived in Egypt.

questions.question: What was the significance of Israel asking Joseph to put his hand under his thigh?
answers: He was asking for help walking
It emphasized a solemn oath or commitment
It signaled that Joseph should leave Egypt
questions.explanation: The gesture was part of a solemn pledge and emphasized that Israel wanted a binding promise.

questions.question: What is the difference between “I will lie with my fathers” and “bury me in their buryingplace”?
answers: The first refers to death, and the second to burial
The first refers to the journey, and the second to the oath
questions.explanation: “Lie with my fathers” is a respectful reference to death, while the second phrase describes burial with the ancestors.

easy.question: Who said, “Swear unto me”?
easy.explanation: Israel asked Joseph to swear to him.

easy.question: To whom did Joseph swear?
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joseph swore to Israel.

easy.question: What did Israel do after Joseph swore to him?
answers: He bowed himself upon the bed’s head
easy.explanation: After Joseph’s oath, Israel bowed himself upon the head of the bed.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Israel asked for an oath, Joseph swore, and Israel bowed
Joseph swore, Israel asked, and Pharaoh bowed
Israel bowed, Joseph asked, and Israel swore
medium.explanation: The exact order is Israel’s request, Joseph’s oath, and Israel’s bowing.

medium.question: In the phrase “Swear unto me,” what does “swear” mean?
answers: Make a solemn promise to me
medium.explanation: Israel was asking Joseph to make a solemn promise concerning his burial.

medium.question: What can be understood from Israel bowing after Joseph swore?
answers: He responded with respect and gratitude
medium.explanation: His bow expressed respect and thanks for Joseph’s agreement.

challenge.question: To whom does “him” refer in “And he sware unto him”?
challenge.explanation: Joseph swore to Israel, who had asked him to make the oath.

challenge.question: Who actually bowed according to the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Israel bowed himself.

challenge.question: Which sentence accurately assigns the actions in the verse?
answers: They both swore to each other
challenge.explanation: The verse assigns the oath to Joseph and the bowing to Israel.

questions.question: To whom does “him” refer in “And he sware unto him”?
questions.explanation: Joseph swore to Israel, who had asked him to make the oath.

questions.question: Who actually bowed according to the verse?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Israel bowed himself.

questions.question: Which sentence accurately assigns the actions in the verse?
answers: They both swore to each other
